verifier_note: Every url re-opened with the kit's fetcher on 2026-10-03; each race checked against sl_races (office and place). Corrected: James Kay's House office cites Wikipedia's June 24, 2013 special election date; Cat Timmerman's website note now says only what the site itself shows (her name and 'running for Louisville Metro Council'; the site does not print District 7 or a paid-for line, and the party page beside which it was found is not given here). Nelson County's page prints the name in capitals ('KEITH METCALFE, DISTRICT 1 MAGISTRATE').
note: The session's shared web-search allowance was already spent when this part began (one search ran), so candidates were looked for only on official county, city, court and party pages reached directly with the kit's fetcher, and on a few campaign addresses tried by name; many county sites and guessed addresses did not resolve. Party pages that only list a candidate (RPK for Wes Pate and Chris Fugate, Louisville GOP for Cat Timmerman, Fayette Democrats for Perry Scott Gibson, Nelson County Democrats for Keith Metcalfe, Hardin County GOP for Bob Mahanna) are already in ballot/lean/ky_endorsements.json and are not repeated here; the only links those pages give besides Cat Timmerman's are Facebook pages, which are not used. The Secretary of State's county filings list Metro Council District 7 as NONPARTISAN, matching our record, so no review item. votejameskay.com (named on Wikipedia) did not resolve, so no website is recorded for James Kay. Lawrence County's officials page names Roger Lee Jordan as jailer but also carries older entries, so his office is recorded without an end and no official_page is claimed. Hopkinsville's council page shows Jason Bell in Ward 11 and Henderson's fiscal court shows Bill Starks in District 5, so Andrea Santos-Rickard and Noah Robert Mills hold no office found there.
